extracted.intended_audience: researchers applying for and managing Cancer Research UK grants
extracted.subtask_description: High-level guidance and policies for applying to, receiving, and managing research funding from Cancer Research UK, including application systems, budgeting, reporting and policy expectations. Covers spotlight call priorities, eligibility and practical supports (e.g., accessibility, extensions, PPI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research funding objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: We fund research across four primary objectives – discovery, detection, prevention and treatment – to build a deeper understanding of every aspect of cancer that will ultimately lead to longer, healthier lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should align with one or more of these primary objectives and demonstrate how the proposed work contributes to understanding, preventing, detecting or treating cancer and ultimately to improved patient outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility, scheme guidance and assessment criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore our funding scheme pages to find out about eligibility, application guidelines and deadlines, what you’ll be assessed on and any specific terms or conditions that may apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow scheme-specific guidance: check eligibility rules, required documents, deadlines and explicit assessment criteria on each scheme page rather than relying on generic statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: How funding decisions are made
rubrics_metrics.description: We follow a rigorous, fair and transparent process to make sure the research we fund aligns with our research priorities and has the greatest potential to make an impact for patients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are evaluated for alignment with CRUK priorities and potential patient impact; emphasise translational potential, relevance to priorities and likely benefit to patients in your case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to spotlight calls
rubrics_metrics.description: Our spotlight calls highlight key areas where dedicated research efforts can improve patient outcomes. We encourage original, high-quality research proposals to address these areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applying to a spotlight call (e.g., reducing inequalities in early detection; tackling upper gastrointestinal cancers), tailor your application to the specified topic and demonstrate novelty and high quality. Funding is available through existing schemes as detailed in each call.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification of costs (justification appendix)
rubrics_metrics.description: When applying for funding, you must provide clear justification for all costs, including staffing, running expenses and animal costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a clear, itemised justification appendix explaining why each cost is required for the project. Cover staffing, consumables, animal costs and any other budget items according to scheme rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of narrative CVs
rubrics_metrics.description: We offer the opportunity to use narrative CVs in your application. This gives you the opportunity to evidence a wider range of skills, experience and showcase broader contributions in research than a traditional CV format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where allowed, use the narrative CV to demonstrate diverse contributions (leadership, teaching, PPI, outreach, mentorship) and relevant skills rather than relying solely on publication lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using Flexi-Grant online system
rubrics_metrics.description: Our application and award process is completed through our online grants management system, Flexi-Grant. Read our guidance on how to set up an account and manage your application and award online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set up and maintain a Flexi-Grant account, follow the system guidance for submitting applications, responding to requests and managing awards. Do not expect alternative submission routes unless explicitly stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting outputs via Researchfish
rubrics_metrics.description: We use Researchfish to capture the outputs and impacts of your research. We use these submissions to help us monitor progress against our research strategy, understand the impact we're having over time and to spot great case studies that we can share with our supporters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with Researchfish reporting requirements: regularly submit outputs, outcomes and impacts as requested. Use these records to demonstrate progress and facilitate CRUK monitoring and publicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify CRUK on submission of publications
rubrics_metrics.description: If you receive funding from us, you need to let us know when you submit a paper or other research results. Doing this before publication gives us time to think about how we might be able to help you promote your research and maximise its impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform CRUK at submission time (not only at publication) so they can consider promotion and impact opportunities; follow any communication channels or forms specified by CRUK.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered reports funding partnership (opt-in)
rubrics_metrics.description: By opting in to our registered reports funding partnership, you can publish results irrespective of your findings and have the opportunity to receive peer review feedback before you even begin your project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider opting into the registered reports pathway to secure in-principle acceptance and peer review of study plans before data collection, supporting publication regardless of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process for grant extensions or suspensions
rubrics_metrics.description: We know things don’t always go to plan and you may have unforeseen delays to your research. If this happens, you may be able to apply to extend or suspend your funding from us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If delays occur, follow CRUK's process to request extensions or suspensions promptly, providing justification and revised timelines as required by the awards management guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disability and accessibility support expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: We want all of our researchers to thrive. Read our guidance and support if you’re applying for or holding Cancer Research UK funding and are disabled or have a long-term health condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage with CRUK's disability/accessibility guidance early in application or award management to identify reasonable adjustments, support options and any implications for project delivery or costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible research careers policy
rubrics_metrics.description: We recognise the challenges you might face managing a research career alongside other responsibilities. Our flexible funding policies are designed to accommodate your circumstances and help you reach your full research potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where relevant, use CRUK's flexible funding provisions (e.g., part-time working, career breaks) and describe any adjustments or support needs in your application and award management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient and public involvement (PPI) expectations and toolkit
rubrics_metrics.description: Patient involvement can improve the quality and relevant[ity] of your research for cancer patients. Our toolkit provides guidance, tips and templates to help you plan, deliver and evaluate your patient involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate appropriate PPI into study design and delivery where relevant; use CRUK's toolkit for practical guidance and to document PPI activities in applications and reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with grant terms, policies and host institution expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Along with the terms in your grant award letter, we also have additional requirements and funding policies governing all grants. Find out more about our policies and expectations for you and your host institution to follow when applying for or holding our funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read and comply with award letter terms plus CRUK-wide policies (e.g., governance, ethics, data sharing, intellectual property and institutional responsibilities). Ensure host institution agreement with these expectations.
